question:
Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

119 + 11 × 5 – 153 ÷ 17 = 201
solution:
**BODMAS rule:**

 [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/1GCDVOWNBvTYyOVoC65TWS6H9eXCmSfFv43DaVimInnSL6_AX5JJ_LMMstUoEomvXAD2-bD6iEvdpHfubOqPNhpszHj65xIZE_DVupuIGiMrDqy-i173FmUE10S9sPknA_qwHadrFc-L0DlnQcAroQ] 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 17 and 5. So the equation will become:

⇒ 119 + 11 × 17 - __**153 ÷ 5**__ = 201

⇒ 119 + **__11 × 17 __**- 30.6 = 201

⇒ __**119 + 187**__ - 30.6 = 201

⇒ 306 - 30.6 = 201

⇒ 275.4 ≠ 201

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

Option 2) 119 and 17. So the equation will become:

⇒ 17 + 11 × 5 - __**153 ÷ 119**__ = 201

⇒ 17 + __**11 × 5 **__- 1.2857 = 201

⇒ __**17 + 55 **__- 1.2857 = 201 

⇒ __**72 - 1.2857 **__= 201

⇒ 70.7143 ≠ 201

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

Option 3) 119 and 153. So the equation will become:

⇒ 153 + 11 x 5 - __**119 ÷ 17**__ = 201

⇒ 153 + __**11 x 5**__ - 7 = 201

⇒ __**153 + 55**__ - 7 = 201

⇒ __**208 - 7**__ = 201

⇒ **201 = 201**

⇒ **LHS = RHS**

Option 4) 11 and 17. So the equation will become:

⇒ 119 + 17 × 5 - __**153 ÷ 11**__ = 201

⇒ 119 + **__17 × 5 __**- 13.90 = 201

⇒ __**119 + 85 **__- 13.90 = 201

⇒ 204 - 13.90 = 201

⇒ 190.1 ≠ 201

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

Hence, the correct answer is **"119 and 153".**
